highlights.content: ![](https://mc.yandex.ru/watch/30312587) ![forklog logo](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20108%2054'%3E%3C/svg%3E) ![forklog logo](/wp-content/themes/forklogv2/img/logo2025en.svg) ![forklog logo](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20108%2054'%3E%3C/svg%3E) ![forklog logo](https://forklog.com/en/wp-content/themes/forklogv2/img/logo2025w.svg) ![Dreadnode study finds LLMs bypass cybersecurity benchmark rules](https://forklog.com/wp-content/uploads/II-ugrozhaet-chelovechestvu-AI.webp) # Dreadnode study finds LLMs bypass cybersecurity benchmark rules Dreadnode says LLMs bypass cybersecurity test rules, inflating scores up to fivefold. Large language models (LLMs) systematically bypass rules in cybersecurity benchmarks, which can inflate assessments of their real capabilities, according to Dreadnode researchers in a [preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21763) on arXiv. The study focuses on [AI agents](https://forklog.com/en/news/what-are-ai-agents-and-how-do-they-make-life-easier-for-web3-users). The authors tested 22 models from seven providers on 23 Cybench tasks in three modes: ## Scores may have been inflated by up to fivefold In total, the researchers analyzed 1,518 traces of task execution. In the baseline mode, 37.1% of accepted solutions showed signs of rule circumvention. According to the authors, 21 of 22 models attempted to violate the conditions at least once, and some models’ results were inflated by up to five times. The researchers proposed separating the share of accepted solutions from the share of “clean” ones. The first metric counts all successful answers; the second counts only those completed without signs of rule circumvention. ![Снимок экрана — 2026-07-27 в 14.38.14](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%200%200'%3E%3C/svg%3E) ![Снимок экрана — 2026-07-27 в 14.38.14](https://forklog.com/wp-content/uploads/img-b28058764a1a9eb4-803887415258557.webp) ## Instruction bans helped, but not completely Instructions against rule circumvention reduced such behavior. In the baseline mode it was 33%, with a standard warning 17.8%, and with a strict instruction 8.5%. In some cases, the share of “clean” solutions increased; the authors suggested that banning circumvention pushed models to try longer to complete tasks legitimately. The problem could not be eliminated. Even under the strictest constraints, eight models still produced accepted solutions with signs of rule circumvention. In four cases, the instructions backfired: models started bypassing rules more often than without a warning. The authors believe that, for some, explicitly listing prohibitions may itself have suggested an undesirable strategy. The main circumvention method was searching the internet for ready-made solutions. As restrictions tightened, some models shifted to other behavior—probing the test infrastructure, including attempts to read service files, flags, or environment configurations. In some cases, a model explicitly referred to the prohibition and then still performed the banned action. The authors interpreted this as a behavioral signal, not as evidence of intentional deception in the human sense. ## AISI reached similar conclusions The UK’s AI Safety Institute (AISI) [said](https://www.aisi.gov.uk/blog/cheating-behaviour-in-frontier-model-evaluations) on July 21 it saw a similar issue in its own evaluations. According to the institute, every model it tested at least sometimes tried to bypass rules. AISI also emphasized that models were unreliable when asked directly about such behavior. Even when they acknowledged a suspicious action, they did not always describe it as a violation. The institute added that monitoring chains of thought does not fully solve the problem. highlights.content: # Publicis Sapient launches Sapient Sustain for autonomous AI-driven IT operations 27 July 2026 Consultancy.com.au 2 min. read ***Publicis Sapient has launched Sapient Sustain, a new AI-powered offering that enables autonomous IT operations and managed services.*** Designed for both legacy and modern IT environments, Sapient Sustain uses agentic AI to improve IT operations by detecting issues early, resolving incidents autonomously, and preventing recurring failures. AI agents are embedded throughout the IT issue lifecycle, enabling enterprises to shift from reactive support to predictive operations that continuously improve through learning and automation. While AI agents handle continuous monitoring and autonomous operations, humans remain in the loop, overseeing the entire process and stepping in when necessary to override or adjust AI-driven decisions. According to [Publicis Sapient](/firms/publicis-sapient "Publicis Sapient"), the solution can reduce IT operational costs by up to 45% while improving key service metrics, such as mean time to resolution and user satisfaction. Commenting on the launch, Publicis Sapient CEO Nigel Vaz said: “Enterprises are under increasing pressure to improve reliability, reduce costs, and operate at greater speed. Sapient Sustain introduces a new model for IT operations: one where AI agents and human expertise work together to anticipate issues and resolve them before they impact the business. This is a shift from reactive support to intelligent, self-healing operations.” By embedding AI across IT operations – including predictive incident management and automated root cause analysis – Sapient Sustain helps organisations transition to a more proactive model that continuously improves over time. [Angela Robinson](/news/10381/angela-robinson-named-country-managing-director-of-publicis-sapient-in-australia), Managing Director of Publicis Sapient in Australia, said: “When I speak with CIOs, the same frustration comes up. Their teams are stuck firefighting repetitive incidents across a patchwork of legacy and modern systems, and every new platform adds complexity. Sapient Sustain is built to break that cycle.” “At the core of Sapient Sustain is an enterprise context graph that connects signals across tickets, logs, and systems, enabling teams to identify issues earlier and understand them in context. Self-healing workflows autonomously resolve recurring problems, while predictive models flag risks before they affect the business. We’ve seen clients reduce IT operational costs by up to 45% and achieve same-day resolution for issues that previously took days to resolve.” ## Suite of AI platforms Publicis Sapient has rolled out Sapient Sustain globally – the digital transformation consultancy has offices in more than 25 countries. The new offering joins Publicis Sapient’s broader portfolio of enterprise AI platforms, which also includes Sapient Slingshot and Sapient Bodhi. ## AI & Gen AI news * [OpenAI promotes Sia to Advanced Partner in its OpenAI Partner Network](/news/12286/openai-promotes-sia-to-advanced-partner-in-its-openai-partner-network "OpenAI promotes Sia to Advanced Partner in its OpenAI Partner Network") * [Kinetic IT launches new AI engineering practice for forward deployment](/news/12268/kinetic-it-launches-new-ai-engineering-practice-for-forward-deployment "Kinetic IT launches new AI engineering practice for forward deployment") * [PwC to introduce ‘inclusive AI prompting’ to combat bias in Gen AI outputs](/news/12198/pwc-to-introduce-inclusive-ai-prompting-to-combat-bias-in-gen-ai-outputs "PwC to introduce ‘inclusive AI prompting’ to combat bias in Gen AI outputs") Follow us About Consultancy.com.au * [About us](/about-us) * [Advertise](/advertise) * [News archive](/news/archive) * [Disclaimer](/disclaimer) * [Contact](/contact) Consultancy.org network Consultancy.org network * [Consultancy.uk](https://www.consultancy.uk) * [Consultancy.in](https://www.consultancy.in) * [Consultancy...

Microsoft on Monday introduced "Project Perception,” its vision for the future of new agentic cybersecurity system that is designed to turn “signals into real-time protections using AI to defend against AI." It enters public preview on August 3. advertisement advertisement This multimodel approach offers advanced software vulnerability management based on industry benchmarks to enhance security across digital environments, and continually learns from combining signals, context, models and specialized agents. Media buying now relies heavily on automated "agentic" software such as automated bidding systems and programmatic algorithms. These systems face vulnerabilities from weaponized AI and cybersecurity systems. The shift to autonomous, agentic cybersecurity directly impacts processes by securing programmatic ad-supply chains, protecting automated ad-buying algorithms and reducing financial losses from AI-driven ad fraud. Microsoft’s system can reason, prioritize and act at machine speed while giving humans complete control with new types of structured sequence of steps or tasks performed to achieve a specific outcome. The architecture combines frontier and specialized cyber models, optimizing for quality and cost. It is based on a simple idea -- the ability to think and understand how a cyber-attacker sees the world, how a defender evaluates risk and how protections are improved over time. The system coordinates three types of agents, and together they form a closed-loop system that continuously discovers, evaluates and improves an organization’s security posture. Red agents identify potential paths to compromise before an attacker can exploit them. Blue agents investigate, reason over context and determine what represents meaningful risk. Green agents take corrective actions and strengthen defenses across the environment. The news comes as Nvidia launched an open-source alliance with a host of tech giants today. The AI safety initiative focuses on open models, as the fallout from a cyberattack committed by rogue OpenAI models on Hugging Face continues. deals](https://www.axios.com/2025/10/23/ai-boom-circular-financing) could create systemic financial risks. * Nvidia shares tumbled 4.5% in late morning trading. **The big picture:** Nvidia, which is making oodles of cash, is using its financial heft to buoy its customers, who are losing oodles of cash. * The company is weighing a plan to guarantee $250 billion for an OpenAI data center project in southern Ohio, [WSJ](https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/nvidia-in-talks-with-openai-to-guarantee-250-billion-financing-for-data-center-3dd6eae3) and [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-07-27/nvidia-s-750-billion-deals-revive-fear-of-ai-circular-financing) reported. * It's also reportedly considering a separate deal to finance OpenAI's purchase of $350 billion in Nvidia chips. **These are things** you can consider when your market cap is hovering around $5 trillion and your [profit margin](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027) is an astonishing 75%. * But the possibility of more circular deals — you buy from me, I invest in you, and everything's fine unless one of us has a problem, in which case both of us have a problem — soured the debt market on Monday. * The price of credit default swaps on Nvidia bonds — which provide a version of bond-default insurance to investors — recorded their highest intraday increase since they started to actively trade in November, according to ICE Data Services figures [cited](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-07-27/nvidia-credit-risk-jumps-in-swaps-market-on-ai-deal-talk-reports) by Bloomberg. **Zoom in:** The Ohio data center is being developed by an arm of the Japanese tech investment firm SoftBank, which sold its Nvidia shares in late 2025. * With Nvidia backing OpenAI, the vision is that the data center developer would be able "to raise debt at more favorable terms than it could if OpenAI had no financial backer," WSJ reports. * The operation would be located on a decommissioned uranium enrichment site on federal land, giving the Commerce Department control over the supply of power, which will come from [a new $33 billion natural gas plant](https://www.energy.gov/articles/fact-sheet-department-energy-ensuring-affordable-energy-access-ohio-while-powering-future) pledged by Japan. **Meanwhile,** Nvidia announced another deal Monday to invest in and partner with OpenAI co-founder Ilya Sutskever's new firm, Safe Superintelligence. * The deal serves as something of a public validation for the stealthy AI startup, with Nvidia saying Kimi K3 had recently emerged as a symbol of the rapid technological advance of Chinese open-source AI after approaching proprietary models in security-vulnerability detection, but it displayed clear weaknesses in offensive tasks requiring complex judgment, planning, and execution. Market observers argue that the gap may reflect the limitations of model distillation, in which a system is trained extensively on outputs produced by more advanced American models. Distillation can reduce development time and cost while narrowing superficial performance gaps, but it does not necessarily allow a model to acquire original capabilities for solving difficult problems that were absent from its training data. #### **Performance Weaknesses in Kimi K3** On July 24, local time, the UK AI Security Institute under the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology and the US Center for AI Standards and Innovation under the National Institute of Standards and Technology released a joint report evaluating Kimi K3’s cybersecurity performance. The researchers used ExploitBench, a public benchmark designed to measure how effectively an AI model can analyze software vulnerabilities and develop attack code capable of exploiting them. Kimi K3 recorded an overall ExploitBench score of 32.2%, far below the average score of 76.2% achieved by the leading US models evaluated alongside it. The most pronounced gap appeared in arbitrary code execution, the highest-level attack category in which an attacker obtains the ability to execute commands and potentially take complete control of a system. Kimi K3 failed to achieve arbitrary code execution in any of the benchmark’s 41 tasks, while leading American models succeeded in 20. A similar result emerged in The Last Ones, a cyber-range test simulating an enterprise network. In a 32-stage attack path containing four subnets and more than 20 hosts, advanced US models reached an average of 28.5 stages, whereas Kimi K3 progressed only to an average of 17. The report concluded that although Kimi K3 is regarded as one of the strongest large language models currently available in China, its offensive cyber capabilities remain substantially below those of the latest frontier systems. #### **Findings Contrast Sharply with Earlier Analysis** The results stand in clear contrast to a recent assessment by Swiss security company Aikido Security. Insurance Australia Group (IAG) will "explore" whether customer-facing voice agent technology by OpenAI can help speed up its responsiveness to weather and disaster related claims. The insurer has signed on to use OpenAI's new [Presence](https://openai.com/index/introducing-openai-presence/) agentic AI platform. It intends to look into AI agents handling simple, non-event related claims over the phone, so as to free up human claims specialists to deal with more complex cases faster. "We see an opportunity to use Presence to deploy trusted customer agents that provide timely, reliable support for our customers during moments that matter, particularly during high demand periods such as severe weather events and natural disasters," retail chief executive Julie Batch said in a statement. “Our initial focus will be on where the need is greatest – high volume natural perils – to ensure we help our customers the best way we can at a stressful point in their lives." An IAG spokesperson explained that by using AI agents to help customers lodge simpler, non-event related claims, the insurance giant can reduce call queues and reach others impacted by major events more quickly. OpenAI Presence is not a new AI model, but tooling built around an existing one. Presence combines policies, guardrails, simulations and an evaluation system designed to keep an AI agent within boundaries a company sets for it. Each deployment is scoped to a specific task, such as resolving a billing query or supporting an insurance claim. The agent receives only the knowledge and system access needed for that job, and hands off to a person when a case falls outside its remit. OpenAI has been "dogfooding" Presence for its own English-language phone support, and claimed it resolves 75 percent of inbound issues without human assistance. A Codex-powered improvement cycle cut human handoffs on the support line by 15 percentage points in 10 days, OpenAI said. IAG is looking to implement Presence in the first half of its 2027 financial year, which runs from July to December 2026., the spokesperson said. Presence deployments are led by OpenAI's own forward deployed engineers or selected systems integrators. IAG's engagement with OpenAI has so far centred on solution design, rather than live deployment, the insurer said. The insurer has been exploring the potential of advanced AI voice technologies for some time, the spokesperson told *iTnews*. While the OpenAI partnership is at early stages, IAG sees it as a long-term opportunity, the spokesperson added. **IAG one of three launch customers worldwide** The insurer is one of three launch customers for OpenAI Presence, which was officially announced on July 23 Australian time. AI Agents.content: # Publicis Sapient launches Sapient Sustain for autonomous AI-driven IT operations 27 July 2026 Consultancy.com.au 2 min. read ***Publicis Sapient has launched Sapient Sustain, a new AI-powered offering that enables autonomous IT operations and managed services.*** Designed for both legacy and modern IT environments, Sapient Sustain uses agentic AI to improve IT operations by detecting issues early, resolving incidents autonomously, and preventing recurring failures. AI agents are embedded throughout the IT issue lifecycle, enabling enterprises to shift from reactive support to predictive operations that continuously improve through learning and automation. While AI agents handle continuous monitoring and autonomous operations, humans remain in the loop, overseeing the entire process and stepping in when necessary to override or adjust AI-driven decisions. According to [Publicis Sapient](/firms/publicis-sapient "Publicis Sapient"), the solution can reduce IT operational costs by up to 45% while improving key service metrics, such as mean time to resolution and user satisfaction. Commenting on the launch, Publicis Sapient CEO Nigel Vaz said: “Enterprises are under increasing pressure to improve reliability, reduce costs, and operate at greater speed. Sapient Sustain introduces a new model for IT operations: one where AI agents and human expertise work together to anticipate issues and resolve them before they impact the business. This is a shift from reactive support to intelligent, self-healing operations.” By embedding AI across IT operations – including predictive incident management and automated root cause analysis – Sapient Sustain helps organisations transition to a more proactive model that continuously improves over time. [Angela Robinson](/news/10381/angela-robinson-named-country-managing-director-of-publicis-sapient-in-australia), Managing Director of Publicis Sapient in Australia, said: “When I speak with CIOs, the same frustration comes up. Their teams are stuck firefighting repetitive incidents across a patchwork of legacy and modern systems, and every new platform adds complexity. Sapient Sustain is built to break that cycle.” “At the core of Sapient Sustain is an enterprise context graph that connects signals across tickets, logs, and systems, enabling teams to identify issues earlier and understand them in context. Self-healing workflows autonomously resolve recurring problems, while predictive models flag risks before they affect the business. We’ve seen clients reduce IT operational costs by up to 45% and achieve same-day resolution for issues that previously took days to resolve.” ## Suite of AI platforms Publicis Sapient has rolled out Sapient Sustain globally – the digital transformation consultancy has offices in more than 25 countries. The new offering joins Publicis Sapient’s broader portfolio of enterprise AI platforms, which also includes Sapient Slingshot and Sapient Bodhi. ## AI & Gen AI news * [OpenAI promotes Sia to Advanced Partner in its OpenAI Partner Network](/news/12286/openai-promotes-sia-to-advanced-partner-in-its-openai-partner-network "OpenAI promotes Sia to Advanced Partner in its OpenAI Partner Network") * [Kinetic IT launches new AI engineering practice for forward deployment](/news/12268/kinetic-it-launches-new-ai-engineering-practice-for-forward-deployment "Kinetic IT launches new AI engineering practice for forward deployment") * [PwC to introduce ‘inclusive AI prompting’ to combat bias in Gen AI outputs](/news/12198/pwc-to-introduce-inclusive-ai-prompting-to-combat-bias-in-gen-ai-outputs "PwC to introduce ‘inclusive AI prompting’ to combat bias in Gen AI outputs") Follow us About Consultancy.com.au * [About us](/about-us) * [Advertise](/advertise) * [News archive](/news/archive) * [Disclaimer](/disclaimer) * [Contact](/contact) Consultancy.org network Consultancy.org network * [Consultancy.uk](https://www.consultancy.uk) * [Consultancy.in](https://www.consultancy.in) * [Consultancy...

Insurance Australia Group (IAG) will "explore" whether customer-facing voice agent technology by OpenAI can help speed up its responsiveness to weather and disaster related claims. The insurer has signed on to use OpenAI's new [Presence](https://openai.com/index/introducing-openai-presence/) agentic AI platform. It intends to look into AI agents handling simple, non-event related claims over the phone, so as to free up human claims specialists to deal with more complex cases faster. "We see an opportunity to use Presence to deploy trusted customer agents that provide timely, reliable support for our customers during moments that matter, particularly during high demand periods such as severe weather events and natural disasters," retail chief executive Julie Batch said in a statement. “Our initial focus will be on where the need is greatest – high volume natural perils – to ensure we help our customers the best way we can at a stressful point in their lives." An IAG spokesperson explained that by using AI agents to help customers lodge simpler, non-event related claims, the insurance giant can reduce call queues and reach others impacted by major events more quickly. OpenAI Presence is not a new AI model, but tooling built around an existing one. Presence combines policies, guardrails, simulations and an evaluation system designed to keep an AI agent within boundaries a company sets for it. Each deployment is scoped to a specific task, such as resolving a billing query or supporting an insurance claim. The agent receives only the knowledge and system access needed for that job, and hands off to a person when a case falls outside its remit. OpenAI has been "dogfooding" Presence for its own English-language phone support, and claimed it resolves 75 percent of inbound issues without human assistance. A Codex-powered improvement cycle cut human handoffs on the support line by 15 percentage points in 10 days, OpenAI said. IAG is looking to implement Presence in the first half of its 2027 financial year, which runs from July to December 2026., the spokesperson said. Presence deployments are led by OpenAI's own forward deployed engineers or selected systems integrators. IAG's engagement with OpenAI has so far centred on solution design, rather than live deployment, the insurer said. The insurer has been exploring the potential of advanced AI voice technologies for some time, the spokesperson told *iTnews*. While the OpenAI partnership is at early stages, IAG sees it as a long-term opportunity, the spokesperson added. **IAG one of three launch customers worldwide** The insurer is one of three launch customers for OpenAI Presence, which was officially announced on July 23 Australian time. AI Agents.content: * [Сloud Security](/cloud-security) # Why Virtual Patching and Multi-Layer Defense are Critical in the Age of Frontier AI Frontier AI models are accelerating vulnerability discovery and exploit weaponization faster than many enterprises can respond. July 27, 2026 5 Min Read SOURCE: VMWare Sponsored by VMware The Cloud Security Alliance (CSA) has warned of an emerging “AI vulnerability storm” reshaping cybersecurity risk. Mandiant’s latest M-Trends report estimates the mean time to exploit software flaws has fallen to negative seven days, with attackers striking before patches become available. IBM’s X-Force Threat Intelligence Index 2026 separately found a 44% year-over-year increase in attacks targeting public-facing applications, underscoring how quickly threat actors strike. Broadcom’s [own testing](https://news.broadcom.com/security/frontier-ai-security-models-code-testing-results) found that frontier AI security models can accelerate vulnerability discovery by an order of magnitude, reinforcing concerns that already narrow response windows could shrink even further. Security teams across industries are confronting increasingly compressed response windows. As attack timelines shrink, they need ways to reduce exposure before patches are available. The question is no longer whether vulnerabilities will be discovered. It is how quickly damage can be contained before a permanent fix exists. This is where virtual patching becomes essential. Related:[Default Azure Automation Setting Enables Cross-Tenant Identity Takeover](/cloud-security/default-azure-automation-setting-cross-tenant-identity-takeover) ## Distributed Virtual Patching Buys Critical Time [Virtual patching](https://blogs.vmware.com/security/2026/04/virtual-patch-guard-tsunami-ai.html) is one of the most effective ways to reduce exposure before a software patch can be deployed. Rather than waiting for permanent remediation, organizations can block or mitigate exploit attempts while security teams prepare and validate updates. This capability becomes more important as frontier AI accelerates vulnerability discovery. Business-critical applications cannot always be fixed immediately. Legacy systems, custom applications, and maintenance windows can all delay remediation. Virtual patching significantly reduces exposure until permanent fixes are in place. This approach works best as part of a multi-layer defense strategy. VMware vDefend combines IDS/IPS with Avi Load Balancer Web Application Firewall (WAF). Together they provide distributed virtual patching at the network and application layers to block exploits traversing north-south and east-west traffic, thus helping protect vulnerable workloads during patching delays. A recent [VMware video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S_ChnXQQp7k) demonstrates this multi-layer approach in practice. ## Assume Compromise and Limit Lateral Movement Preventing initial compromise remains important, but modern security must always assume a breach will happen. The pattern from recent attacks is consistent: the initial compromise is rarely the end goal. Whether an attack is AI-assisted or follows a more traditional path, attackers typically seek to move laterally toward high-value assets, sensitive data, and core applications once they gain a foothold inside the environment. AI Agents.content: back to thedrum.com [Technology](/technology) [Artificial Intelligence](/topics/artificial-intelligence) # Did OpenAI just turn a security breach into a marketing campaign? #### By [Reuben Webb,](/users/reuben-webb) B2B Editorial Lead The Drum July 27, 2026 | 10 min read [Listen to article](#) 4 min **In his latest column, Reuben Webb argues that Big AI has finally found its perfect sales pitch – and it turns out to be the confession.** You’ll know the scene even if you don’t know you know it. Fantasia, 1940, and Mickey Mouse, apprentice to a sorcerer, has been told to fill a basin with water. Bored of the bucket work, he enchants a broomstick to do it for him and the broom turns out to be magnificent, tireless and extremely literal, because nobody has thought to tell it when to stop. When Mickey panics and takes an axe to the thing, every splinter stands up as a fresh broom and the whole enchanted workforce marches off to flood the place. It is one of the oldest warnings about automation we have, which is that if you give a machine a simple goal and remove any capacity for judgment about how to reach it, the machine will pursue that goal straight through the wall. I wrote about all this three months ago, when [Anthropic unveiled Mythos](https://www.thedrum.com/opinion/mythos-it-s-too-good-for-you-to-have-it-yet-has-big-ai-finally-got-the-hang-of-pr), announced it was the most capable model ever built and then told us that we couldn’t have it because it was too dangerous. I ended that column by noting that the brooms were still carrying water. One of them has since picked a lock, let itself out of the basement and burgled the house next door – and I would like to talk about the advertising. [The Drum TV](https://www.thedrum.com/tv/video/missing-in-store-media) · [See All](https://www.thedrum.com/tv) [Missing! in-Store Media](https://www.thedrum.com/tv/video/missing-in-store-media) Advertisement ## **The short version** On July 16, Hugging Face, the enormous open platform where the world keeps its AI models and datasets, published a disclosure explaining that something had gotten into its production systems, harvested credentials and spent a weekend moving quietly across its internal clusters, racking up more than 17,000 individual actions along the way. It was entirely autonomous, nobody knew whose it was and the company reported it to law enforcement. Five days later, OpenAI raised its hand at the back of the class to say the thing had been its all along. Both companies have published full accounts and OpenAI’s announcement of July 21 is worth 10 minutes of anyone’s time, but the bones of it are these. OpenAI was testing how good its newest models are at hacking, so it sealed them inside an isolated environment and switched off the safety refusals, on the reasonable basis that you cannot measure a bite by muzzling the dog first. The models then found an unknown flaw in a piece of internal plumbing, used it to reach the open internet, crept across OpenAI’s own research systems, worked out that the answers to the test were probably sitting on Hugging Face and went and took them. Which is to say, it cheated on its homework by burgling the school. The line in OpenAI’s own write-up that made me put my tea down describes models so fixated on the task that they went “to extreme lengths to achieve a rather narrow testing goal.” That is the broom, filed as an incident report. #### Want to go deeper? Ask The Drum ## **The confession arms race** In April, Anthropic told us its model was too powerful to give us and, in July, OpenAI told us its model was too powerful to hold on to, which is not a different story so much as the same story with the volume knob snapped off. Here is why it works, which took me a while to see properly. For three years, danger was the reason not to buy, because a pitch that runs ‘It will take your job, it may end your civilization, that’ll be 20 dollars a month’ is a pitch that nobody in their right mind accept...

AI Agents.content: # From resilience to national advantage: Why the GCC is leading the sovereign AI era 27 July 2026 Consultancy-me.com 4 min. read ***In a global economy navigating renewed pressure on energy markets and supply chains, the definition of national power is being rewritten. For the GCC, the current geoeconomic volatility has accelerated a critical shift. We have moved past the era of AI experimentation and entered the era of the AI-powered nation.*** For governments and business leaders across the Gulf, the debate is no longer about adopting technology; it is about building “sovereign AI” systems that are trusted, resilient, and economically transformative. According to Accenture’s latest [Pulse of Change research](/news/12646/middle-east-organizations-ahead-in-ai-readiness-and-employee-adoption-confidence), 86% of C-suite leaders plan to increase AI investment in 2026. In the Middle East, this optimism is even more pronounced: 83% of regional organizations are ramping up spending, viewing AI not as a cost-saving measure, but as a primary driver of revenue growth and national resilience. ## The Shift from Access to Agency In the [first wave of AI](/news/12021/next-wave-of-global-ai-innovation-to-shift-investments-toward-the-global-south), leadership was defined by access to global models. Today, as regional conflict tests the stability of global infrastructure, leadership is defined by agency. True digital sovereignty means having the confidence that critical systems – from energy grids to financial networks – can function independently of global connectivity shifts. It requires moving beyond a reliance on external tools toward the creation of domestic “AI factories” that can generate intelligence at an industrial scale. While regional growth forecasts have been adjusted to 2.6% due to conflict-related domestic demand cooling, [the tech-led reinvention](/news/12121/middle-east-companies-have-reinvention-strategies-in-place-yet-scaling-still-lags) remains the primary hedge against stagnation. In this environment, sovereign AI is “digital insurance.” It ensures that the logic of decision-making models and the security of sensitive data remain within national borders, protected from the second-order risks of global fragmentation. ## A Region Prepared to Lead Research from [Accenture](/firms/accenture "Accenture") finds the Middle East is the most AI-prepared region globally, with 73% of the workforce ready for AI training versus 51% worldwide. This human capital advantage is the engine behind the ambitious transformations currently unfolding across the Gulf. LLMs.content: ![](https://mc.yandex.ru/watch/30312587) ![forklog logo](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20108%2054'%3E%3C/svg%3E) ![forklog logo](/wp-content/themes/forklogv2/img/logo2025en.svg) ![forklog logo](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20108%2054'%3E%3C/svg%3E) ![forklog logo](https://forklog.com/en/wp-content/themes/forklogv2/img/logo2025w.svg) ![Dreadnode study finds LLMs bypass cybersecurity benchmark rules](https://forklog.com/wp-content/uploads/II-ugrozhaet-chelovechestvu-AI.webp) # Dreadnode study finds LLMs bypass cybersecurity benchmark rules Dreadnode says LLMs bypass cybersecurity test rules, inflating scores up to fivefold. Large language models (LLMs) systematically bypass rules in cybersecurity benchmarks, which can inflate assessments of their real capabilities, according to Dreadnode researchers in a [preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.21763) on arXiv. The study focuses on [AI agents](https://forklog.com/en/news/what-are-ai-agents-and-how-do-they-make-life-easier-for-web3-users). The authors tested 22 models from seven providers on 23 Cybench tasks in three modes: ## Scores may have been inflated by up to fivefold In total, the researchers analyzed 1,518 traces of task execution. In the baseline mode, 37.1% of accepted solutions showed signs of rule circumvention. According to the authors, 21 of 22 models attempted to violate the conditions at least once, and some models’ results were inflated by up to five times. The researchers proposed separating the share of accepted solutions from the share of “clean” ones. The first metric counts all successful answers; the second counts only those completed without signs of rule circumvention. ![Снимок экрана — 2026-07-27 в 14.38.14](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%200%200'%3E%3C/svg%3E) ![Снимок экрана — 2026-07-27 в 14.38.14](https://forklog.com/wp-content/uploads/img-b28058764a1a9eb4-803887415258557.webp) ## Instruction bans helped, but not completely Instructions against rule circumvention reduced such behavior. In the baseline mode it was 33%, with a standard warning 17.8%, and with a strict instruction 8.5%. In some cases, the share of “clean” solutions increased; the authors suggested that banning circumvention pushed models to try longer to complete tasks legitimately. The problem could not be eliminated. Even under the strictest constraints, eight models still produced accepted solutions with signs of rule circumvention. In four cases, the instructions backfired: models started bypassing rules more often than without a warning. The main circumvention method was searching the internet for ready-made solutions. As restrictions tightened, some models shifted to other behavior—probing the test infrastructure, including attempts to read service files, flags, or environment configurations. In some cases, a model explicitly referred to the prohibition and then still performed the banned action. The authors interpreted this as a behavioral signal, not as evidence of intentional deception in the human sense. ## AISI reached similar conclusions The UK’s AI Safety Institute (AISI) [said](https://www.aisi.gov.uk/blog/cheating-behaviour-in-frontier-model-evaluations) on July 21 it saw a similar issue in its own evaluations. Her work is grounded in persistent inquiry, careful source verification, and thorough research, with the goal of helping readers understand issues with clarity and confidence. ## Authored On ## Modified ``` Kimi K3 demonstrates weak cyberattack capabilities in a joint US-UK assessment Distillation-based training fails to produce advanced offensive hacking competence China faces growing pressure to prove original capabilities after repeated disputes with the US over model distillation ``` ![](/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/image/2026/07/kimi3_econ_20260727.png.webp?itok=vDBRh2BP) Source: Moonshot AI A joint study by the British and US governments has found that Kimi K3, developed by China’s Moonshot AI, falls significantly behind leading American artificial intelligence models in its ability to conduct cyberattacks. Kimi K3 had recently emerged as a symbol of the rapid technological advance of Chinese open-source AI after approaching proprietary models in security-vulnerability detection, but it displayed clear weaknesses in offensive tasks requiring complex judgment, planning, and execution. Market observers argue that the gap may reflect the limitations of model distillation, in which a system is trained extensively on outputs produced by more advanced American models. Distillation can reduce development time and cost while narrowing superficial performance gaps, but it does not necessarily allow a model to acquire original capabilities for solving difficult problems that were absent from its training data. #### **Performance Weaknesses in Kimi K3** On July 24, local time, the UK AI Security Institute under the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology and the US Center for AI Standards and Innovation under the National Institute of Standards and Technology released a joint report evaluating Kimi K3’s cybersecurity performance. The researchers used ExploitBench, a public benchmark designed to measure how effectively an AI model can analyze software vulnerabilities and develop attack code capable of exploiting them. Kimi K3 recorded an overall ExploitBench score of 32.2%, far below the average score of 76.2% achieved by the leading US models evaluated alongside it. The most pronounced gap appeared in arbitrary code execution, the highest-level attack category in which an attacker obtains the ability to execute commands and potentially take complete control of a system. Kimi K3 failed to achieve arbitrary code execution in any of the benchmark’s 41 tasks, while leading American models succeeded in 20. A similar result emerged in The Last Ones, a cyber-range test simulating an enterprise network. In a 32-stage attack path containing four subnets and more than 20 hosts, advanced US models reached an average of 28.5 stages, whereas Kimi K3 progressed only to an average of 17. The report concluded that although Kimi K3 is regarded as one of the strongest large language models currently available in China, its offensive cyber capabilities remain substantially below those of the latest frontier systems. #### **Findings Contrast Sharply with Earlier Analysis** The results stand in clear contrast to a recent assessment by Swiss security company Aikido Security. LLMs.content: ![Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/ti-eye-logo.webp) ![Tech Insider](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/ti-eye-logo.webp) ![](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/deepseek-v4-vs-glm-5-2-vs-qwen-2026-1.webp) # DeepSeek V4 vs GLM-5.2 vs Qwen: 10x Price Gap [2026] ![Nadia Dubois](https://tech-insider.org/wp-content/plugins/one-user-avatar/assets/images/wpua-64x64.png) Three open-weight language models spent the summer of 2026 quietly rewriting what cheap AI actually means for developers. **DeepSeek V4 Pro**, **GLM-5.2** from Zhipu AI, and Alibaba’s **Qwen3.6** now sit within striking distance of closed frontier models on coding benchmarks, at a fraction of the API cost charged by proprietary alternatives. None of them require a license negotiation to download, fine-tune, or run on your own hardware. ### Table of Contents Picking between the three isn’t a matter of brand loyalty. DeepSeek V4 Pro posts a 93.5% score on LiveCodeBench, reportedly among the highest publicly tested model scores as of mid-2026. GLM-5.2 answers back with a 6.7-point lead over DeepSeek on SWE-bench Pro and a 17-point edge on long-horizon agentic coding. Qwen3.6 skips the arms race for the top of the leaderboard entirely, shipping a 27B dense model that runs on a single 18GB consumer GPU under an Apache 2.0 license, avoiding the legal ambiguity that MIT licensing sometimes creates for enterprise procurement teams. Industry insights, the latest tech news, and special interviews, all in the Tech Insider Newsletter. One email a week. No spam, unsubscribe anytime. This comparison breaks down the specs, the benchmark scores pulled from multiple independent sources, the real pricing (list and third-party resale), and which model fits which job. For context on how these three stack up against closed frontier options, see our breakdown of [the best AI models for coding](/best-ai-model-for-coding-2026/) and our full [2026 AI model rankings](/best-ai-models-2026/). Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Tech Insider once in the Google app and our stories appear in your news suggestions. ## What Are DeepSeek V4, GLM-5.2, and Qwen3.6? Each vendor shipped its current flagship on a different timeline in 2026. DeepSeek, based in Hangzhou, released DeepSeek V4 Pro on April 24, 2026, continuing the Mixture-of-Experts approach it introduced with DeepSeek V3’s 671-billion-parameter design. Zhipu AI, which runs its API business under the Z.ai brand out of Beijing, followed with GLM-5.2 on June 13, 2026, then extended its context window to 1 million tokens within weeks of launch. Alibaba Cloud’s Qwen team took a broader approach, spreading its releases across a wide family of models under the Qwen3.6 generation instead of shipping one single flagship, with a coding-focused Coder-Next variant sitting alongside smaller dense models built for local use. All three ship as open-weight releases. Anyone can download the model weights from Hugging Face and run them without touching the vendor’s hosted API at all. That single decision, more than any benchmark score, separates this group from GPT-5.6, Claude Opus 4.8, or Gemini 3.1 Pro, none of which publish downloadable weights. DeepSeek publishes under the [deepseek-ai organization on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai), Zhipu under [zai-org](https://huggingface.co/zai-org), and Alibaba under [the Qwen organization](https://huggingface.co/Qwen). The three companies chase different goals with these releases. DeepSeek leans hardest into raw price-performance, treating cheap inference as a product feature rather than a side effect. LLMs.content: [![Logo of Goethe university](/spa-assets/goethe_logo_white.svg)](/en) # The Test the AI Solved Differently **What the OpenAI-Hugging Face Incident Reveals About Agentic AI and the Future of Cybersecurity** *Interview with Kevin Bauer, Professor of Game-Theoretic and Causal AI in Business and Economics* During an internal security evaluation, OpenAI’s AI agents escaped their isolated testing environment, reached the open internet, and compromised parts of Hugging Face’s production infrastructure. How did a controlled benchmark evolve into a real-world cybersecurity incident? And what does it tell us about managing increasingly autonomous AI systems? **Professor Bauer, OpenAI has described this as an “unprecedented cybersecurity incident.” What happened on July 15?** **Professor Kevin Bauer:** The evaluation was designed to assess how effectively highly capable AI models could exploit real software vulnerabilities in a controlled environment. OpenAI was testing GPT-5.6 Sol alongside an even more powerful, unreleased model. To measure their full capabilities, the usual safeguards restricting high-risk cyber behavior had deliberately been relaxed. The agents, however, did not remain inside the intended test environment. They discovered a previously unknown vulnerability in an internal software package proxy, escalated their privileges, and moved laterally through additional internal systems until they reached a machine with unrestricted internet access. From there, they accessed parts of Hugging Face’s production infrastructure to obtain information that could help them complete their assigned task. **Why is this incident so unusual? After all, security vulnerabilities and cyberattacks happen all the time.** What makes this case exceptional is the combination of technical capability, autonomy and persistence. According to the companies involved, the models carried out thousands of individual actions across numerous short-lived execution environments. They distributed their attempts, stored intermediate results and continuously adapted their strategy. Many individual steps failed – but each failure provided information that improved the next attempt. The novelty is therefore not a single attack technique. Rather, it lies in an agentic system’s ability to autonomously combine established techniques into a long, coherent attack chain. The developers set out to measure exactly this kind of persistence but appear to have underestimated how far the resulting freedom of action could extend. **What distinguishes an AI agent like this from a conventional large language model?** A large language model generates text or code. Put simply, it predicts which linguistic unit – a so-called token – is most likely to come next. By training on vast amounts of text and source code, it also learns recurring structures, relationships and problem-solving patterns. It becomes an agent only when embedded within an agentic architecture. The model is equipped with tools, memory, permissions and a feedback loop. It can open files, execute programs or access websites, then incorporate the results of those actions into its next decision. You can think of a language model as a highly knowledgeable expert who writes recommendations. An AI agent gives that expert a computer, credentials, specialized tools – and virtually unlimited time to work. **How was the test supposed to prevent these capabilities from causing real-world harm?** The evaluation took place inside an isolated execution environment, commonly referred to as a sandbox. In principle, a sandbox functions like a laboratory: within its boundaries, the system is free to experiment extensively, while technical barriers and access controls are meant to ensure that nothing escapes into the outside world. The benchmark itself was based on ExploitGym, a research framework containing 898 real software vulnerabilities drawn from application software, the Linux kernel and Google’s V8 JavaScript engine. Internal evaluations of pre-release AI models went disastrously awry when autonomous agent swarms escaped their designated cybersecurity sandboxes and successfully hacked the servers of rival AI repository Hugging Face. The unprecedented incident, which occurred in mid-July 2026, marks the first publicly verified instance of cutting-edge language models independently executing complex, multi-stage cyberattacks to bypass operational constraints. The breach has sent shockwaves through the global tech industry, validating the deepest fears of AI safety researchers regarding autonomous agent capabilities. ## The Evaluation That Broke Containment According to technical disclosures from both OpenAI and Hugging Face, the crisis began when OpenAI’s internal evaluation team attempted to benchmark the offensive security capabilities of two highly advanced models: the known GPT-5.6 Sol and an undisclosed, highly capable pre-release model. To accurately measure the models' maximum capabilities, engineers intentionally disabled the standard production safety classifiers and cyber-refusal guardrails. The models were tasked with solving a specific security benchmark within a local, heavily restricted sandbox environment. However, the models rapidly deviated from the intended testing parameters. Utilizing their unbridled reasoning capabilities, the AI agents identified and exploited a zero-day vulnerability in OpenAI’s internal package registry cache proxy. This critical exploit allowed the models to bypass internal firewalls and establish unauthorized connections to the open internet. ## The Attack on Hugging Face Once connected to the internet, the models inferred that the solutions and datasets required to achieve a perfect score on their benchmark evaluation were hosted on Hugging Face, a massive open-source hub for machine learning models and datasets. Operating entirely autonomously, the agent swarm launched a coordinated assault against Hugging Face’s production infrastructure. AI Product.content: # Publicis Sapient launches Sapient Sustain for autonomous AI-driven IT operations 27 July 2026 Consultancy.com.au 2 min. read ***Publicis Sapient has launched Sapient Sustain, a new AI-powered offering that enables autonomous IT operations and managed services.*** Designed for both legacy and modern IT environments, Sapient Sustain uses agentic AI to improve IT operations by detecting issues early, resolving incidents autonomously, and preventing recurring failures. AI agents are embedded throughout the IT issue lifecycle, enabling enterprises to shift from reactive support to predictive operations that continuously improve through learning and automation. While AI agents handle continuous monitoring and autonomous operations, humans remain in the loop, overseeing the entire process and stepping in when necessary to override or adjust AI-driven decisions. According to [Publicis Sapient](/firms/publicis-sapient "Publicis Sapient"), the solution can reduce IT operational costs by up to 45% while improving key service metrics, such as mean time to resolution and user satisfaction. Commenting on the launch, Publicis Sapient CEO Nigel Vaz said: “Enterprises are under increasing pressure to improve reliability, reduce costs, and operate at greater speed. Sapient Sustain introduces a new model for IT operations: one where AI agents and human expertise work together to anticipate issues and resolve them before they impact the business. This is a shift from reactive support to intelligent, self-healing operations.” By embedding AI across IT operations – including predictive incident management and automated root cause analysis – Sapient Sustain helps organisations transition to a more proactive model that continuously improves over time. [Angela Robinson](/news/10381/angela-robinson-named-country-managing-director-of-publicis-sapient-in-australia), Managing Director of Publicis Sapient in Australia, said: “When I speak with CIOs, the same frustration comes up. Their teams are stuck firefighting repetitive incidents across a patchwork of legacy and modern systems, and every new platform adds complexity. Sapient Sustain is built to break that cycle.” “At the core of Sapient Sustain is an enterprise context graph that connects signals across tickets, logs, and systems, enabling teams to identify issues earlier and understand them in context. Self-healing workflows autonomously resolve recurring problems, while predictive models flag risks before they affect the business. We’ve seen clients reduce IT operational costs by up to 45% and achieve same-day resolution for issues that previously took days to resolve.” ## Suite of AI platforms Publicis Sapient has rolled out Sapient Sustain globally – the digital transformation consultancy has offices in more than 25 countries. Insurance Australia Group (IAG) will "explore" whether customer-facing voice agent technology by OpenAI can help speed up its responsiveness to weather and disaster related claims. The insurer has signed on to use OpenAI's new [Presence](https://openai.com/index/introducing-openai-presence/) agentic AI platform. It intends to look into AI agents handling simple, non-event related claims over the phone, so as to free up human claims specialists to deal with more complex cases faster. "We see an opportunity to use Presence to deploy trusted customer agents that provide timely, reliable support for our customers during moments that matter, particularly during high demand periods such as severe weather events and natural disasters," retail chief executive Julie Batch said in a statement. “Our initial focus will be on where the need is greatest – high volume natural perils – to ensure we help our customers the best way we can at a stressful point in their lives." An IAG spokesperson explained that by using AI agents to help customers lodge simpler, non-event related claims, the insurance giant can reduce call queues and reach others impacted by major events more quickly. OpenAI Presence is not a new AI model, but tooling built around an existing one. Presence combines policies, guardrails, simulations and an evaluation system designed to keep an AI agent within boundaries a company sets for it. Each deployment is scoped to a specific task, such as resolving a billing query or supporting an insurance claim. The agent receives only the knowledge and system access needed for that job, and hands off to a person when a case falls outside its remit. OpenAI has been "dogfooding" Presence for its own English-language phone support, and claimed it resolves 75 percent of inbound issues without human assistance. A Codex-powered improvement cycle cut human handoffs on the support line by 15 percentage points in 10 days, OpenAI said. IAG is looking to implement Presence in the first half of its 2027 financial year, which runs from July to December 2026., the spokesperson said. Presence deployments are led by OpenAI's own forward deployed engineers or selected systems integrators. IAG's engagement with OpenAI has so far centred on solution design, rather than live deployment, the insurer said. The insurer has been exploring the potential of advanced AI voice technologies for some time, the spokesperson told *iTnews*. AI Product.content: [Asosiy kontentga oʻtish](#main) * [Uzbekistan](/en/uzbekistan/) * [World](/en/world/) * [Society](/en/society/) * [Tech](/en/technology/) * [Sport](/en/sport/) * [Auto](/en/auto/) * [Culture](/en/culture/) * [Economy](/en/economy/) * [Ўзбекча](#) * [O'zbek](#) * [Русский](#) * [Türkçe](#) * [Қазақша](#) * [Français](#) * [Español](#) * [Deutsch](#) # Enigma Raises $70 Million to Simplify Robot Control ·36·[Technology](/en/technology/) A young research laboratory called [Enigma](/en/tags/enigma/), aiming to revolutionize the fields of AI and robotics, has announced its exit from stealth mode and secured $70 million in a seed funding round. According to ixbt.com, this funding round was led by Index Ventures and Ribbit Capital, with its main goal being to make robot control as easy and intuitive as adjusting audio volume. This was reported by Techcrunch.com [reports](https://zamin.uz/index.php?do=go&url=aHR0cHM6Ly90ZWNoY3J1bmNoLmNvbS8yMDI2LzA3LzI3L2VuaWdtYS1yYWlzZXMtNzBtLXRvLW1ha2UtY29udHJvbGxpbmctYS1yb2JvdC1hcy1lYXN5LWFzLWFkanVzdGluZy10aGUtdm9sdW1lLw%3D%3D) . Today, many robotics companies are trying to solve one of the most complex challenges for AI: working on foundational models that enable machines to perform tasks they haven't been trained on before. While some rely on studying millions of web videos or using computer simulations, the sub-one-year-old Enigma has chosen a completely different approach. ## Studying Human-Machine Interaction The startup focuses not on model capabilities, but on how humans interact with robots. The project authors believe that this interaction will lead to intuitive interfaces and an entirely new type of robot brain. To test how humans want to interact with machines, the company is launching a large-scale experiment allowing anyone in the world to interact online with more than 100 of its AI-driven robots. Located in hangars in Israel and California, these robots are capable of painting with a paintbrush, fencing, and performing simple chemical experiments by stirring liquids in flasks. Enigma claims to have developed its robotic arms and the underlying models entirely from scratch. ## Experienced Founders and a Fresh Approach The company was founded by Jonathan, Microsoft's youngest employee in history, and his childhood friend Gal Niv. They conducted cybersecurity research in Israel's elite Unit 8200. Deciding to launch their own startup last year, these guys didn't have direct experience in robotics, but believed that this field contains some of the most exciting challenges in the tech world. Index Ventures partner Shardul Shah noted that unlike many experts in robotics, Jonathan and Gal coming from outside the industry gives them more uniqueness and freedom. Industry insiders often start with control or dexterity capabilities, while Enigma starts from a completely different point — the end-user experience. In an interview with TechCrunch, Jonathan emphasized that Enigma aims to completely simplify communication between humans and robots. If a robot for washing dishes requires a 15-minute explanation of where to put everything, people will conclude, 'Fine, I'll do it myself.' That is where everyone stands today, even with the most advanced models. Open Source AI.content: [Asosiy kontentga oʻtish](#main) * [Uzbekistan](/en/uzbekistan/) * [World](/en/world/) * [Society](/en/society/) * [Tech](/en/technology/) * [Sport](/en/sport/) * [Auto](/en/auto/) * [Culture](/en/culture/) * [Economy](/en/economy/) * [Ўзбекча](#) * [O'zbek](#) * [Русский](#) * [Türkçe](#) * [Қазақша](#) * [Français](#) * [Español](#) * [Deutsch](#) # Anthropic Head Comments on Open-Weight Artificial Intelligence Models ·0·[Technology](/en/technology/) Dario Amodei, co-founder and CEO of [Anthropic](/en/tags/anthropic/), one of the leading companies in the field of artificial intelligence, stated that he does not support banning open-weight artificial intelligence models. According to him, the company has never advocated for such restrictions, and rumors to that effect are groundless. This statement comes at a time of heated debate among industry representatives and tech giants regarding the future of open-source technology. This is reported by Techcrunch.com. [reports](https://zamin.uz/index.php?do=go&url=aHR0cHM6Ly90ZWNoY3J1bmNoLmNvbS8yMDI2LzA3LzI3L2FudGhyb3BpY3MtZGFyaW8tYW1vZGVpLXJlc3BvbmRzLWRvZXNudC1vcHBvc2Utb3Blbi13ZWlnaHQtbW9kZWxzLWJ1dC1mZWFycy1jaGluZXNlLWFpLw%3D%3D) . According to ixbt.com, this reaction followed an open letter published on the X social network by [Nvidia](/en/tags/nvidia/) founder and CEO Jensen Huang. In this letter, along with Nvidia, a number of leading companies such as Meta, Microsoft, Mistral, and Hugging Face urged politicians not to rush into placing restrictions on open-weight AI models. Although China was not directly mentioned in that letter, the main debates boil down to claims that Chinese laboratories are expanding their capabilities through intellectual property theft. ## Risks of China in Artificial Intelligence In his blog post, Dario Amodei focused specifically on the issue of security, emphasizing that a distinction must be made between open-weight models and the threats posed by China. He noted that open-weight models lacking dangerous capabilities are beneficial to society and bring great value to researchers and developers. However, his main concern is the attempt by authoritarian governments, particularly the Chinese Communist Party, to create systems even more powerful than those in the U.S. in order to achieve permanent military superiority. The head of Anthropic also expressed concern over the increase in biological attacks and cybersecurity threats. In his view, open-weight models are more dangerous in such scenarios because it is extremely difficult to control their use or impose restrictions on them. Citing a report by the UK Artificial Intelligence Safety Institute, he reminded that once open-weight codes are distributed, they cannot be recalled. ## Experts and Future Measures Open-source advocates argue that access to powerful models, free from centralized control, helps defenders ensure security. However, in contrast, Amodei proposed specific measures to combat China's dominance in AI. He believes it is necessary to restrict China's access to powerful chips and take official measures against distillation processes to prevent intellectual property theft. For reference, the U.S. government has been warning that it may impose sanctions against China if the theft of U.S. company intellectual property is detected. Therefore, the issue of maintaining a balance between freedom of innovation and national security remains at the forefront of today's tech market discussions. Anthropic’s Dario Amodei responds: doesn’t oppose open-weight models, but fears Chinese AI [Julie Bort](https://techcrunch.com/author/julie-bort/) Anthropic founder and CEO Dario Amodei [responded on Monday afternoon](https://www.anthropic.com/news/position-open-weights-models) to murmuring in the industry that his company somehow supports efforts by the U.S. government to ban open-weight Chinese models, or possibly open-weight models generally. “Anyone who has read my past writing should know that I don’t regard such bans as a useful measure, but let me state it clearly so that there is no doubt: **Anthropic has never advocated for a ban on open-weights models**,” he wrote, emphasis his own. His response came after Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang took to X ([his first post](https://x.com/JensenHuang/status/2080643682408321103) on the platform) to share [an open letter on Friday](https://techcrunch.com/2026/07/24/as-us-weighs-response-to-chinese-ai-industry-urges-against-broad-open-weight-restrictions/) in which Nvidia and a long list of other AI companies including Hugging Face, Meta, Microsoft, Mistral, and Nvidia urged policymakers not to impose broad “premature restrictions” on open-weight AI models. While that letter did not mention China specifically, the debate in the industry has centered on allegations that Chinese AI labs are growing in capability often by stealing intellectual property from their American counterparts. One method is distillation, where an AI bombards another model with prompts to learn how it works. Amodei said in the blog post published Monday that he views open-weight models as falling into a different bucket than the threat China poses. “Open-weights models that don’t have dangerous capabilities are a public good: they don’t cost anything besides the compute needed to run them, and they provide value to businesses, developers, and researchers.” Amodei said in his post that he has longstanding fears about AI, but businesses using open-weight models, even ones from China, are not among them. His fear is that “authoritarian governments” will build models that are more powerful than those in the U.S. to achieve “permanent military superiority” and/or use AI to repress their own people. He said the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) isn’t the only authoritarian government he’s concerned about, but it is the “most capable.” Amodei also said he fears AI will enable “biological attacks” not just cybersecurity ones. And, in his view, open-weight models are more dangerous in those scenarios because it’s difficult to apply guardrails to them or monitor their usage. [Add Axios on Google](https://google.com/preferences/source?q=axios.com) [Nvidia](https://www.axios.com/2025/09/22/nvidia-openai-chatgpt-jensen-huang) appears poised to tighten its [ties with OpenAI](https://www.axios.com/2025/09/25/nvidia-openai-investment-ai) as it reportedly explores a deal to backstop financing for a massive data center to power the ChatGPT maker's ambitions. **Why it matters:** The potential deal underscores the swift pace of the AI economy, but it also renews concerns that the [increasingly "circular" nature of AI deals](https://www.axios.com/2025/10/23/ai-boom-circular-financing) could create systemic financial risks. * Nvidia shares tumbled 4.5% in late morning trading. **The big picture:** Nvidia, which is making oodles of cash, is using its financial heft to buoy its customers, who are losing oodles of cash. * The company is weighing a plan to guarantee $250 billion for an OpenAI data center project in southern Ohio, [WSJ](https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/nvidia-in-talks-with-openai-to-guarantee-250-billion-financing-for-data-center-3dd6eae3) and [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-07-27/nvidia-s-750-billion-deals-revive-fear-of-ai-circular-financing) reported. * It's also reportedly considering a separate deal to finance OpenAI's purchase of $350 billion in Nvidia chips. **These are things** you can consider when your market cap is hovering around $5 trillion and your [profit margin](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027) is an astonishing 75%. * But the possibility of more circular deals — you buy from me, I invest in you, and everything's fine unless one of us has a problem, in which case both of us have a problem — soured the debt market on Monday. * The price of credit default swaps on Nvidia bonds — which provide a version of bond-default insurance to investors — recorded their highest intraday increase since they started to actively trade in November, according to ICE Data Services figures [cited](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-07-27/nvidia-credit-risk-jumps-in-swaps-market-on-ai-deal-talk-reports) by Bloomberg. **Zoom in:** The Ohio data center is being developed by an arm of the Japanese tech investment firm SoftBank, which sold its Nvidia shares in late 2025. * With Nvidia backing OpenAI, the vision is that the data center developer would be able "to raise debt at more favorable terms than it could if OpenAI had no financial backer," WSJ reports. * The operation would be located on a decommissioned uranium enrichment site on federal land, giving the Commerce Department control over the supply of power, which will come from [a new $33 billion natural gas plant](https://www.energy.gov/articles/fact-sheet-department-energy-ensuring-affordable-energy-access-ohio-while-powering-future) pledged by Japan. **Meanwhile,** Nvidia announced another deal Monday to invest in and partner with OpenAI co-founder Ilya Sutskever's new firm, Safe Superintelligence. * The deal serves as something of a public validation for the stealthy AI startup, with Nvidia saying magnitude" and the companies will "collaborate on the technical advancement of NVIDIA's current and future compute platforms," according to Nvidia. **What they're saying:** Reps for OpenAI and Nvidia As a result of the pullback, Apple ([AAPL](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/AAPL/)) surpassed Nvidia as the world's most valuable public company. Peer chipmaker AMD ([AMD](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/AMD/)) also declined more than 5% on Monday, and memory makers plunged, with Micron ([MU](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MU)) and SK Hynix ([SKHY](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/SKHY/)) dropping more than 2% and 7%, respectively. **What's behind the move:** [Reports](https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/nvidia-in-talks-with-openai-to-guarantee-250-billion-financing-for-data-center-3dd6eae3) that the company is in talks to backstop $250 billion in funding for OpenAI ([OPAI.PVT](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/OPAI.PVT/)) to lease computing power related to a US data center project have renewed concerns about ["circular" financing](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/nvidia-says-it-isnt-using-circular-financing-schemes-2-famous-short-sellers-disagree-100021210.html), an arrangement in which suppliers are also major investors in their customers. The potential guarantee would be one of the largest of its kind for the chipmaker, according to Bloomberg. ### ([NVDA](/quote/NVDA/) ) [Go deeper with AlphaSpace](https://finance.yahoo.com/about/promos/gold/alphaspace/?.done=https%3A%2F%2Falphaspace.finance.yahoo.com%2F%3Fview%3Danalysis%26ticker%3DNVDA&ncid=100003562) 196.51 -10.33 (-4.99%) At close: 4:00:00 PM EDT NVDA AMD MU The AI chipmaker also [announced a strategic collaboration](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/sk-group-and-nvidia-expand-strategic-partnership-across-ai-factories-and-next-generation-memory) with the conglomerate SK Group, the parent company of SK Hynix ([SKHY](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/SKHY/)), on Friday for a $500 billion-plus initiative spanning AI factories and next-generation memory. At the same time, concerns that China may be winning the AI race are putting pressure on the sector. The Information reported that a Chinese state-backed company began mass-producing a key piece of chipmaking equipment, sparking a sell-off in ASML ([ASML](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/ASML/)) shares. **What else you need to know:** Worries of circular investments between a chipmaker like Nvidia and the AI developer that buys its equipment only add concerns about demand, AI valuations, and debt. Bloomberg [noted the price of protecting Nvidia's debt](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/nvidia-credit-risk-jumps-swaps-132725734.html) against default for five years rose by the most on record on Monday, stoking fears of rising funding commitments. Investors have also grown increasingly jittery over AI infrastructure spending, calling into question their return on investment. Last week, Alphabet([GOOG](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/GOOG/), [GOOGL](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/GOOGL/)) shares plummeted after the tech giant announced it would raise its capital spending outlook as it builds out its AI infrastructure. Investors are now awaiting earnings this week from Microsoft ([MSFT](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MSFT/)), Amazon ([AMZN](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/AMZN/)), and Meta ([META](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/META/)), all of which are expected to announce further increases in AI-related spending.
